title: Change in fiber intake in children and adolescents with celiac disease before and after initiation of a gluten-free diet
summary:
Celiac disease is caused by an immune reaction to gluten (e.g. from wheat or other grains) which damages the lining of the small intestine.. This makes it harder for the body to absorb nutrients from food. At this time the only treatment for celiac disease is to avoid foods containing gluten, which limits the variety of foods that can be consumed. The gluten-free diet might also lead to an insufficient intake of fiber.
The aim of this study is to investigate the influence of a gluten-free diet on the amount of consumed fiber and how the eating habits of celiac patients change before and after starting a gluten-free diet. Furthermore, we hope to gain insights into the influence of a gluten-free diet on bone metabolism, as changes in bone metabolism are often associated with celiac disease.

interventions.name: Group A: Patients with newly diagnosed celiac disease; haven't started gluten free diet yet
Group B: Patients who have already been diagnosed with celiac disease; started gluten free diet 3 months ago (10-16 weeks)
Group C: Patients who have already been diagnosed with celiac disease; started gluten free diet at least 1 year ago
Group D: Age- and gender-matched patients from the pediatric and adolescent gastroenterology consultation without celiac disease
Group E: Healthy siblings of patients from groups A-D

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Group A: newly diagnosed celiac disease in accordance with guidelines while consuming a gluten-containing diet
(histological and/or serological)
• Group B: celiac disease diagnosed in accordance with guidelines and strict gluten-free diet
for 3 months (10–16 weeks)
• Group C: Celiac disease diagnosed in accordance with guidelines and strict gluten-free diet
for at least 12 months
• Group E: Maximum age difference between siblings of 3 years
Exclusion criteria:
• Lack of consent from legal guardians and patients
• Lack of language comprehension
• Age under 3 years
• Other accompanying chronic inflammatory bowel diseases
• Diabetes mellitus type I/II
• Psoriasis
• Fructose malabsorption
• Other concomitant diseases requiring long-term medication
• Parenteral nutrition
• Group A: gluten-free diet already started before inclusion in the study
• Groups D and E: diagnosed celiac disease or indication of existing celiac disease,
gluten-free diet
